why: All three refutation grounds were tested and none holds. (1) QUOTE — verbatim. curl -sL of env-vars.md puts the sentence at line 78, word for word. Read whole: line 78 is four sentences, and the remaining three only add caveats (a startup-only reader such as OpenTelemetry keeps its startup values; removing a variable does not unset it in a running session) — they do not reverse the conclusion. The page's own lines 89-98 give the four-scope table (user / project / local / managed) and lines 104-112 give the override-the-shell and re-apply-on-change semantics the finding restates, so the CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR is a fair reading, not an inflation. env-vars is row 101 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so the citation is against a real Claude Code contract page. (2) CITED LINES — two of three exact. managed-policy.ts:359 is literally 'readonly env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>'; project-config.ts:138 is literally the FORBIDDEN_SECTIONS line carrying 'env', 'environment'. validators.ts:521 is off by five lines (it is authType); the MCP stdio env record the finding means is at validators.ts:526. Wrong line, right construct — not a substantive refutation. (3) CONSEQUENCE — verified separately from the identifier, by four independent absence checks with -a: the user config file ~/.nessy-agent/config.json (config/storage.ts:152) and config-defaults.json (config-defaults-schema.ts) carry no env key; there is no dotenv/loadEnvFile anywhere in apps/ or packages/; apps/cli has no --env flag; and agent/claude-settings-store.ts — the one module that touches .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json and ~/.claude/settings.json — is a WRITE-ONLY permission-rule store whose own test asserts it merge-PRESERVES an env block it never reads (claude-settings-store.test.ts:81). permissions-config.ts:419 confirms the read side: a Claude settings file is recognised for its permissions block and nothing else. Not an owner decision: inert-worklist section 3's nine dated decisions do not include this. Not a product difference either — this is not a rename, not a dropped subscription flow, not gateway scoping. Two partial substitutes exist and neither closes it: apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts spawns the login shell and imports its environment at Electron startup, which answers the doc's stated MOTIVATION (they take effect no matter how claude was launched) but is macOS-only, skipped in dev mode, cannot set a variable absent from the profile, and cannot override one; and the network variables the docs single out as belonging in the env block are typed user-scope settings instead (NetworkProxySettings, config/types.ts:27), where refusing an env-block merge is a RECORDED security property (plans/2026-07-28-network-trust-chain.md Task 4). The headless nessy-server has neither mitigation — that plan records its trust as the plain shell-env contract — so for it the gap is unmitigated. The finding survives, but narrowed: see correctedState.
correctedState: Narrow the finding to USER and LOCAL scope; two of the four scopes it implies are wrong. MANAGED scope is implemented, including the live re-apply the claim treats as missing: managed-policy.ts:359 declares the block, config/managed-env.ts:330 applyManagedEnv applies it under a four-category withhold rule, and config/managed-delivery.ts startManagedDeliveryEnvApplication re-applies on every later state change without a restart (the host-owned policy FILE applies with source 'managed-file' and is never withheld). PROJECT scope is a recorded security refusal, which the finding itself concedes: 'env' and 'environment' are in FORBIDDEN_SECTIONS (plugins/project-config.ts:138), diagnosed at severity error and never applied. What is genuinely absent is user and local scope: no env key in ~/.nessy-agent/config.json (config/storage.ts:152) or config-defaults.json, no dotenv loader, no CLI --env flag, and no reader of the env block in .claude/settings.json — agent/claude-settings-store.ts touches those files only as a write destination for permission rules. Every other env record in the tree is per-server or per-command rather than session-wide: MCP stdio (config/validators.ts:526, not :521), hook commands (automations/schemas.ts:72), plugin MCP (plugins/types.ts:187). Partial mitigations, neither sufficient: apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts imports the login shell environment on macOS at Electron startup (skipped in dev; cannot add or override a variable), and the network subset (proxy, tlsCaPath, certStore, mTLS) is typed user config in NetworkProxySettings (config/types.ts:27) by recorded decision. The headless nessy-server has no mitigation at all.
